title: Previous-year flow raised nitrate plus nitrite estimation error at two Gulf river outlets in yearly tests for 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether previous-year discharge improved estimates of measured filtered nitrate plus nitrite at the Mississippi River near St. Francisville and the Atchafalaya River at Melville. We used USGS release 3.0 and 767 site-dates in held-out water years 2000-2025. Each model used the preceding 20 water years. The baseline used current flow, season and trend. The added model used log mean flow over the preceding 365 days and its interaction with current flow. Added flow history raised mean relative squared log error by 4.22%. The conditional 95% common-year block interval was an increase of 1.36% to 7.14%. Separate site increases were 3.50% and 4.94%. All six planned model settings had higher point error. Omitting any one test year left higher mean error. Added corrections tended to point away from the remaining baseline errors. These results give no useful gain for the tested predictor. They do not exclude physical nutrient memory or gains from other models. The two branches are related. Sparse samples, source revisions, flow-gauge locations, model choice and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The package gives numeric source extracts, exact hashes, code, all estimates and draws, a separate numerical audit, figures and repeat instructions.

display.caption: Previous-year flow raised sample estimation error at both sites in the primary test. Upper panels show yearly squared log error. Lower panels show error reduction, so negative values mean higher error. Bars give conditional 95% common-year block intervals. The tests use 767 site-dates in water years 2000-2025 from USGS release 3.0. The intervals hold source observations and fitted estimates fixed.

citations.reason: We reuse the fixed shared source archive and consult its R-date extraction recipe. The present test uses observed sample concentration and yearly holdouts, not annual model-derived loads. The source observations overlap.
USGS source release, version 3.0, May 27, 2026. Exact source and member hashes, observation fields and retrieval URLs are supplied.
Prior work links earlier flow and nitrate anomalies at selected Mississippi basin sites. The present test examines yearly transfer of a specified estimator at two outlet sites.
Prior methods add flow-history terms to concentration and flux models. The present result tests one limited form and does not refute these wider methods.
Prior high-frequency observations in the lower Mississippi show large nitrate changes during the 2012 drought and 2013 flood.
